metadata.title: Investigational New Drug Application Submissions for Individualized Antisense Oligonucleotide Drug Products for Severely Debilitating or Life-Threatening Diseases: Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Recommendations, Guidance for Sponsor-Investigators : Draft Guidance for Industry
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.statement: The purpose of this guidance is to provide recommendations regarding the chemistry, 18 manufacturing, and controls (CMC) information that should be provided in an investigational 19 new drug application (IND) submitted by a sponsor-investigator 2 (hereafter referred to as 20 sponsor) developing an individualized antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) drug product for a 21 severely debilitating or life-threatening (SDLT) disease 3 caused by a unique genetic variant 22 where only a small number of individuals are prospectively identified (typically one or two). 23 These individualized ASO drug products should be from a well-characterized chemical class for 24 which there is substantial clinical and nonclinical experience that is either publicly available or to 25 which the sponsor has a right to reference. 4
candidates.context: This guidance is limited to those individualized ASO drug products, as described above, that are 28 unconjugated, manufactured using conventional methods, with formulations that are a simple 29 aqueous or a lyophilized powder to be reconstituted before administration. 30

candidates.statement: Studies of Drugs, Including Well-Characterized, Therapeutic, Biotechnology-Derived Products 75 (November 1995). 8 That guidance includes clarification about the data that should be provided 76 in the CMC section of an initial IND submission under 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7). FDA expects 77 sponsors to submit in the CMC section of an initial IND sufficient information to ensure the 78 proper identification, quality, purity, and strength of the investigational drug product. This 79 information includes (1) data and information regarding drug substance; (2) data and information 80 regarding drug product; (3) the investigational drug immediate packaging label that includes the 81 statement “Caution: New Drug — Limited by Federal (or United States) law to investigational 82 use”; 9 and (4) a statement requesting a categorical exclusion from an environmental assessment 83 under 21 CFR 25.30 or 25.31 or an environmental assessment under 21 CFR 25.40. 10
candidates.context: This guidance provides recommendations about how to satisfy these general requirements for the 86 CMC content of an IND for an investigational ASO drug product within the scope of this 87 guidance and also provides specific recommendations regarding the quality (e.g., chemical 88 structure, manufacturing process, and critical quality attributes) of an individualized ASO drug 89 product that will be administered to an individual trial participant under the IND. To expedite 90 the initiation of clinical investigation of an individualized ASO drug product covered under this 91 guidance, we recommend that the sponsor first submit a pre-IND meeting request to discuss the 92 CMC plans with FDA. 93

candidates.statement: To expedite the initiation of clinical investigations of these individualized ASO drug products, 134 we recommend that, when possible, the same batch of drug product used for the nonclinical 135 studies be used for initial clinical investigations. 12 If different batches of the drug product are 136 intended for nonclinical studies and clinical investigations, the sponsor should provide 137 information to support a conclusion that the batch used in the nonclinical studies is representative 138 of the batch intended for use in the clinical investigations, from a quality perspective. This 139 information should include a description of any differences in the manufacturing processes 140 between the nonclinical and clinical batches, as well as analytical data establishing that the 141 nonclinical batch is representative of the batch to be administered to the subject(s). 142

candidates.statement: The sponsor must provide a description of the drug substance, which should include the 165 structure, nomenclature, structural formula, molecular formula, molecular weight, and molecular 166 weight of the salt form (if applicable). In addition, the sponsor should provide a statement 167 regarding the nature of base moieties and backbone, carbohydrate moieties, internucleoside 168 linkages, and counter ions (if applicable) that constitute the structure of the individualized ASO 169 drug substance. The sponsor should provide information about the physical properties such as 170 hygroscopicity, solubility in aqueous media, and the melting temperature (Tm) (if relevant). 171

candidates.statement: The sponsor should confirm the chemical structure of the drug substance using physical and 206 chemical techniques, including nucleotide sequencing, Tm, and mass spectral analysis. The 207 sponsor should provide the sequence determination of an ASO drug substance; however, if the 208 sequence determination is not provided in the initial IND, the sponsor should include an 209 adequate justification in the IND and submit the sequence in an amendment as soon as possible. 210 The sponsor should provide information on impurities in the ASO drug substance. The sponsor 211 should summarize the actual and potential impurities most likely to arise during manufacture, 212 purification, and storage of the drug substance. FDA recommends that sponsors list ASO-related 213 impurities and, when appropriate, group them based on their structural class or relative retention 214 times. 215
candidates.context: The sponsor should provide a discussion related to the occurrence of non-ASO related impurities 217 (e.g., elemental impurities, residual solvents, protecting groups) and how control of these 218 impurities is ensured. The submission should include specifications for observed non-ASO 219 related impurities or a scientific justification for why such testing would not be required (e.g., 220 description of the step(s) included in the manufacturing process to remove certain non-ASO 221 related impurities). 222

candidates.statement: The sponsor should monitor the stability of the individualized ASO drug product packaged in the 338 proposed container closure system under the proposed storage conditions. The sponsor should 339 provide the stability protocol for the clinical batch, including a brief description of the stability 340 study and the test methods, with a commitment to monitor stability of the drug product 341 throughout its use. If initial stability data for the clinical batch are available, the sponsor should 342 provide the data in tabular format. If stability data for the clinical batch are not available, the 343 sponsor should provide any available supportive stability data (e.g., data from the nonclinical 344 batch, if different from the clinical batch; data from a laboratory batch). 345

candidates.context: If the individualized ASO drug product is modified before use (e.g., reconstituted or diluted for 347 infusion), the drug product, ready for administration (e.g., in the infusion bag), should not be 348 stored at room temperature for longer than 4 hours or under refrigerated conditions for longer 349 than 24 hours to minimize the risk for excessive growth of adventitious microbial contamination. 350

candidates.statement: However, if extended storage conditions are necessary, the sponsor should conduct 352 microbiological studies supporting the postconstitution/postdilution storage time (as stated in the 353 proposed product labeling) as recommended in the ICH guidances for industry Q8(R2) 354 Pharmaceutical Development (November 2009) 25 and Q1A(R2) Stability Testing of New Drug 355 Substances and Products (November 2003). 26 The submission should include a description of 356 the test methods and results of studies that are designed using a minimum countable inoculum 357 (less than or equal to 100 colony forming units (CFU)/ milliliter (mL)) to simulate potential 358 microbial contamination that may occur during drug product constitution or dilution. 359 Additionally, the sponsor should justify the selected test conditions and/or diluents as necessary. 360 Challenge organisms can include strains described in USP General Chapter <51> in addition to 361 typical skin flora, species associated with nosocomial infection, or psychrophilic organisms. The 362 sponsor should provide a positive control that demonstrates the viability of the organisms over 363 the duration of the test period. 364
